rows.38:6e54:
Hmm, you're no fun...
Well, they do say it's better not to go near it carelessly, just out of curiosity.
Like, say you touched that cherry tree, right?
They say the skin where you touched it breaks out in a rash.
At first it just puffs up a little, but nothing you put on it makes it heal, and in the end it festers into an oozing mess. That's what I've heard.
There was someone before who touched the tree out of curiosity, and their skin festered, and they couldn't stand it anymore and cut that spot off with a box cutter.{p}
rows.38:72c4:
They say schools are places where spirits gather easily.
Because that tree is pulling in the spirit paths, I think all the wandering spirits around here are gathering there too.
They say that with Kokkuri-san too, low-level spirits and animal spirits are easier to call, right?
I can't tell what kind of spirit paths run through it, but I feel like I can kind of sense a swirl of psychic energy centered on the cherry tree.
Whenever I look at that tree, I get goosebumps.
Somewhere far off in the back of my mind, an alarm goes off.
That tree is dangerous!
They say it's still on the quiet side for now.
But one of these days... the grudges of the spirits, stored up to their limit, will burst into bloom.
With malice riding on every single petal...
When that time comes, what's going to happen to this school, I wonder?
It might be tomorrow, or it might be a year from now.
Or maybe it's already...{p}
rows.38:81d0:
They say there used to be a small lake around here.
That cherry tree supposedly stood on the shore of that lake, so the old school building would have been completely underwater.
Nature worship, I guess you'd call it?
It's a faith that's been around in Japan since way back, and that lake and the cherry tree were worshipped by the people back then too.
It was a local folk faith, so I think it was something simple.
Prayers for a good harvest, praying for rain, and festivals of thanks...
Ordinary stuff you'd find anywhere, right?
Loved by simple people, they must have spent their days in peace.
Yes, until that time came...{p}
rows.38:6888:
So you didn't actually see anything.
But you can tell this tree isn't just an ordinary cherry tree, right?
You can tell from the blossoms alone, but there's a lot more around it, things the eye can't see.
There might be loads of faces full of grudges showing up on that trunk, too...{p}
